# **TalentRank Assessment: Complete Question Bank**

## **Document Purpose**

This document provides a complete, scientifically-grounded question bank for the TalentRank assessment. All questions are either public domain, validated, or original items based on established psychological constructs. This document is designed to be handed to a developer/assessment designer for implementation.

---

## **Assessment Overview**

| Section | Questions | Time | Purpose |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1\. Personality Wiring | 32 questions | 5-6 min | Big Five → MBTI-style type |
| 2\. Self-Sabotage Patterns | 15 questions | 3-4 min | Identify limiting behaviors |
| 3\. Optimal Environment | 12 questions | 2-3 min | Work/culture fit |
| 4\. Cognitive Architecture | 16 questions | 10-15min (timed) | IQ/processing estimate |
| 5\. Short Answer | 6 questions | 3-4 min | AI report personalization |

---

# **SECTION 1: PERSONALITY WIRING (32 Questions)**

## **Scientific Basis**

* Source: IPIP Big-Five Factor Markers (Goldberg, 1992\)  
* License: **Public Domain** — free to use, modify, translate without permission  
* Reliability: Cronbach's alpha \= 0.79-0.87 per dimension  
* Citation: Goldberg, L. R. (1992). The development of markers for the Big-Five factor structure. *Psychological Assessment, 4*, 26-42.

## **Big Five → MBTI Mapping**

| Big Five Dimension | MBTI Axis | Mapping |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Extraversion | E/I | Direct (High E \= E) |
| Openness/Intellect | N/S | High Openness \= N |
| Agreeableness | T/F | Inverted (Low A \= T) |
| Conscientiousness | J/P | High C \= J |
| Neuroticism | (separate) | Used for stress resilience metric |

## **Response Scale**

5-point Likert: 1 \= Very Inaccurate, 2 \= Moderately Inaccurate, 3 \= Neutral, 4 \= Moderately Accurate, 5 \= Very Accurate

---

### **EXTRAVERSION / INTROVERSION (8 questions)**

*Maps to E/I axis*

| \# | Question | Keying | Source |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| P1 | I am the life of the party. | E+ | IPIP |
| P2 | I don't talk a lot. | I+ (reverse) | IPIP |
| P3 | I feel comfortable around people. | E+ | IPIP |
| P4 | I keep in the background. | I+ (reverse) | IPIP |
| P5 | I start conversations. | E+ | IPIP |
| P6 | I have little to say. | I+ (reverse) | IPIP |
| P7 | I talk to a lot of different people at parties. | E+ | IPIP |
| P8 | I am quiet around strangers. | I+ (reverse) | IPIP |

**Scoring:**

* Sum E+ items (P1, P3, P5, P7) directly  
* Reverse score I+ items (P2, P4, P6, P8): 6 minus response  
* Total possible: 8-40  
* Midpoint: 24  
* Score \> 24 \= E, Score \< 24 \= I  
* Strength: |Score \- 24| / 16 × 100%

---

### **OPENNESS / INTUITION vs SENSING (8 questions)**

*Maps to N/S axis*

| \# | Question | Keying | Source |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| P9 | I have a rich vocabulary. | N+ | IPIP |
| P10 | I have difficulty understanding abstract ideas. | S+ (reverse) | IPIP |
| P11 | I have a vivid imagination. | N+ | IPIP |
| P12 | I am not interested in abstract ideas. | S+ (reverse) | IPIP |
| P13 | I have excellent ideas. | N+ | IPIP |
| P14 | I do not have a good imagination. | S+ (reverse) | IPIP |
| P15 | I am quick to understand things. | N+ | IPIP |
| P16 | I spend time reflecting on things. | N+ | IPIP |

**Scoring:**

* Sum N+ items directly  
* Reverse score S+ items: 6 minus response  
* Score \> midpoint \= N, Score \< midpoint \= S

---

### **AGREEABLENESS (Inverted \= Thinking/Feeling) (8 questions)**

*Maps to T/F axis — LOW Agreeableness \= Thinking, HIGH Agreeableness \= Feeling*

| \# | Question | Keying | Source |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| P17 | I am interested in people. | F+ | IPIP |
| P18 | I feel little concern for others. | T+ (reverse) | IPIP |
| P19 | I sympathize with others' feelings. | F+ | IPIP |
| P20 | I insult people. | T+ (reverse) | IPIP |
| P21 | I have a soft heart. | F+ | IPIP |
| P22 | I am not interested in other people's problems. | T+ (reverse) | IPIP |
| P23 | I take time out for others. | F+ | IPIP |
| P24 | I make people feel at ease. | F+ | IPIP |

**Scoring:**

* High score \= Feeling (F)  
* Low score \= Thinking (T)  
* Note: This is inverted from typical Big Five interpretation

---

### **CONSCIENTIOUSNESS (8 questions)**

*Maps to J/P axis — HIGH Conscientiousness \= Judging, LOW \= Perceiving*

| \# | Question | Keying | Source |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| P25 | I am always prepared. | J+ | IPIP |
| P26 | I leave my belongings around. | P+ (reverse) | IPIP |
| P27 | I pay attention to details. | J+ | IPIP |
| P28 | I make a mess of things. | P+ (reverse) | IPIP |
| P29 | I get chores done right away. | J+ | IPIP |
| P30 | I often forget to put things back in their proper place. | P+ (reverse) | IPIP |
| P31 | I like order. | J+ | IPIP |
| P32 | I shirk my duties. | P+ (reverse) | IPIP |

**Scoring:**

* High score \= Judging (J)  
* Low score \= Perceiving (P)

---

### **NEUROTICISM / EMOTIONAL STABILITY (Optional \- 6 questions)**

*Does not map to MBTI but useful for stress resilience metric*

| \# | Question | Keying | Source |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| N1 | I get stressed out easily. | N+ | IPIP |
| N2 | I am relaxed most of the time. | ES+ (reverse) | IPIP |
| N3 | I worry about things. | N+ | IPIP |
| N4 | I seldom feel blue. | ES+ (reverse) | IPIP |
| N5 | I get upset easily. | N+ | IPIP |
| N6 | I change my mood a lot. | N+ | IPIP |

**Use:** Generate "Stress Resilience" score for the report. High neuroticism \= lower stress resilience.

## **Personality Section Output (IMPORTANT NOTE \- THIS WILL ALL BE AT THE END)**

**Primary Output:** 4-letter type (e.g., INTJ)

**Secondary Output:** Axis strengths

* "Strong I (85%)" vs "Slight I (55%)"  
* This differentiates from competitors who only show binary types

**Example Result:**

Type: INTJ  
I: 78% (Strong Introvert)  
N: 92% (Very Strong Intuitive)  
T: 61% (Moderate Thinker)  
J: 54% (Slight Judger)  
Stress Resilience: 42% (Moderate)

# **SECTION 2: SELF-SABOTAGE PATTERNS (15 Questions)**

## **Scientific Basis**

Questions adapted from validated scales:

* Self-Handicapping Scale (Rhodewalt, 1990\)  
* Clance Impostor Phenomenon Scale (Clance, 1985\) — *Note: Clance requires permission for commercial use; questions below are inspired by construct but reworded*  
* Procrastination Assessment Scale (Solomon & Rothblum, 1984\)  
* Frost Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale concepts

## **Response Scale**

5-point Likert: 1 \= Never, 2 \= Rarely, 3 \= Sometimes, 4 \= Often, 5 \= Very Often

---

### **PERFECTIONISM PARALYSIS (3 questions)**

| \# | Question | Construct |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| S1 | I delay starting projects because I'm not sure I can do them perfectly. | Perfectionism \+ Procrastination |
| S2 | I spend so much time planning that I don't have enough time to execute. | Analysis Paralysis |
| S3 | I abandon projects when I realize they won't meet my standards. | Perfectionism |

---

### **IMPOSTOR PATTERNS (3 questions)**

*Inspired by Clance construct, original wording*

| \# | Question | Construct |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| S4 | When I succeed, I attribute it more to luck or timing than my abilities. | External Attribution |
| S5 | I'm afraid people will discover I'm not as capable as they think. | Fear of Exposure |
| S6 | I downplay my accomplishments when others praise me. | Discounting Success |

---

### **SELF-HANDICAPPING (3 questions)**

*Adapted from Self-Handicapping Scale concepts*

| \# | Question | Construct |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| S7 | Before important tasks, I find reasons why I might not perform well. | Excuse Preparation |
| S8 | I put less effort into things that matter so I have an excuse if I fail. | Effort Withdrawal |
| S9 | I take on too much so I can blame poor performance on being overcommitted. | Overcommitment Excuse |

---

### **VALIDATION SEEKING (3 questions)**

| \# | Question | Construct |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| S10 | I check with others before making decisions I could make myself. | External Validation |
| S11 | Criticism from others affects my confidence more than it should. | External Locus |
| S12 | I avoid stating opinions until I know what others think. | Approval Seeking |

---

### **RISK / CONFLICT AVOIDANCE (3 questions)**

| \# | Question | Construct |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| S13 | I stay in situations I've outgrown because change feels risky. | Risk Aversion |
| S14 | I avoid difficult conversations even when they're necessary. | Conflict Avoidance |
| S15 | I'd rather keep the peace than advocate for what I want. | Self-Suppression |

---

## **Sabotage Pattern Scoring**

**Calculate subscale scores:**

* Perfectionism Paralysis: (S1 \+ S2 \+ S3) / 3  
* Impostor Pattern: (S4 \+ S5 \+ S6) / 3  
* Self-Handicapping: (S7 \+ S8 \+ S9) / 3  
* Validation Seeking: (S10 \+ S11 \+ S12) / 3  
* Avoidance Pattern: (S13 \+ S14 \+ S15) / 3

**Thresholds:**

* Score ≥ 3.5: Primary pattern (feature prominently in report)  
* Score 2.5-3.5: Secondary pattern (mention in report)  
* Score \< 2.5: Not a significant pattern

**Output Labels (user-facing):**

| Pattern | Label | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Perfectionism Paralysis | "The Perfectionist" | You over-prepare and under-execute |
| Impostor Pattern | "The Doubter" | You discount your wins and fear exposure |
| Self-Handicapping | "The Hedger" | You create excuses before you even try |
| Validation Seeking | "The Approval Seeker" | You outsource your confidence |
| Avoidance Pattern | "The Conflict Avoider" | You prioritize comfort over growth |

# **SECTION 3: OPTIMAL WORK ENVIRONMENT (12 Questions)**

## **Scientific Basis**

* Holland RIASEC concepts (public domain theory)  
* IIP RIASEC Markers (Armstrong, Allison, & Rounds, 2008\) — free for non-commercial research  
* Person-Environment Fit theory

## **Response Scale**

5-point scale with labeled endpoints (varies by question)

---

### **AUTONOMY vs STRUCTURE (3 questions)**

| \# | Question | Scale |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| E1 | I prefer work where I set my own priorities and methods. | 1 \= Strongly Disagree → 5 \= Strongly Agree |
| E2 | I work better with clear guidelines and defined processes. | 1 \= Strongly Disagree → 5 \= Strongly Agree |
| E3 | How much direction do you prefer from managers? | 1 \= Complete Autonomy → 5 \= Detailed Guidance |

**Scoring:**

* High E1, Low E2, Low E3 \= High Autonomy preference  
* Low E1, High E2, High E3 \= High Structure preference

---

### **PACE PREFERENCE (2 questions)**

| \# | Question | Scale |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| E4 | I thrive in fast-paced environments with tight deadlines. | 1 \= Strongly Disagree → 5 \= Strongly Agree |
| E5 | I do my best work when I can take time to be thorough. | 1 \= Strongly Disagree → 5 \= Strongly Agree |

---

### **SOCIAL DENSITY (3 questions)**

| \# | Question | Scale |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| E6 | I prefer working independently most of the time. | 1 \= Strongly Disagree → 5 \= Strongly Agree |
| E7 | I feel energized by collaborating with a team throughout the day. | 1 \= Strongly Disagree → 5 \= Strongly Agree |
| E8 | My ideal work involves: | 1 \= Mostly Solo → 5 \= Mostly Team |

---

### **RISK TOLERANCE (2 questions)**

| \# | Question | Scale |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| E9 | I prefer stable positions over high-upside but uncertain opportunities. | 1 \= Strongly Disagree → 5 \= Strongly Agree |
| E10 | I'm willing to take a pay cut for work that's more meaningful to me. | 1 \= Strongly Disagree → 5 \= Strongly Agree |

---

### **WORK MODE (2 questions)**

| \# | Question | Scale |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| E11 | I do my best work: | 1 \= Fully Remote → 3 \= Hybrid → 5 \= Fully In-Person |
| E12 | I prefer environments that are: | 1 \= Quiet/Focused → 5 \= Buzzing/Social |

---

## **Environment Section Output**

**Primary Output:** Environment Profile

Example:

Optimal Environment:  
• Autonomy: High (prefers self-direction)  
• Pace: Fast (thrives under pressure)  
• Social: Mixed (solo work with collaborative moments)  
• Risk Tolerance: High (comfortable with uncertainty)  
• Work Mode: Hybrid-leaning-remote

**Career Fit Indicators:** Based on responses, map to environment types:

* High Autonomy \+ High Pace \+ High Risk \= Startup / Entrepreneurship  
* High Structure \+ Low Risk \+ High Social \= Large Corporate  
* High Autonomy \+ Low Pace \+ Low Social \= Creative/Research  
* etc.

# **SECTION 5: SHORT ANSWER / OPEN-ENDED (6 Questions)**

## **Purpose**

These questions feed directly into the AI system that generates personalized reports. They elicit specific, revealing information that the structured questions cannot capture.

## **Question Design Principles**

1. **Behavioral specificity** — ask about real situations, not hypotheticals  
2. **Projective elements** — indirect questions reveal more than direct ones  
3. **Emotional valence** — touch on fears and aspirations  
4. **Manageable length** — users should be able to answer in 2-4 sentences

---

### **Questions**

| \# | Question | What It Reveals |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| O1 | What do you do for work, and what's the hardest part of your job? | Current context \+ pain points |
| O2 | If you knew you couldn't fail, what would you do with your career? | Aspirations \+ risk barriers |
| O3 | What do people misunderstand about you? | Self-perception \+ identity |
| O4 | What's a goal you've had for over a year that you haven't achieved? Why not? | Sabotage patterns \+ self-awareness |
| O5 | Describe a recent situation where you felt frustrated at work. | Behavioral data \+ triggers |
| O6 | When you imagine "making it," what does that look like? | Success definition \+ values |

---

### **Optional Projective Questions (can rotate or A/B test)**

| \# | Question | What It Reveals |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| O7 | If you were a shape, what would you be and why? | Abstract self-concept |
| O8 | What do you fear people say about you behind your back? | Core insecurities |
| O9 | Describe yourself in three words. Now describe how others would describe you. | Self vs. perceived identity |

# **IMPLEMENTATION NOTES FOR DEVELOPER**

## **Question Presentation**

1. **Randomize within sections** — don't show all E/I questions together  
2. **Alternate positive/negative keyed items** — prevents response sets  
3. **Progress indicator** — show "Section 2 of 5" and question count  
4. **Mobile optimization** — especially critical for cognitive section

## **Timing (Cognitive Section)**

// Example timer logic  
const COGNITIVE\_TIME\_LIMIT \= 360; // 6 minutes in seconds  
let timeRemaining \= COGNITIVE\_TIME\_LIMIT;

// Show soft warning at 1 minute remaining  
// Allow completion after time expires but flag in data  
// Record time per question for potential analysis

## **Data Storage**

Store for each user:

* Raw responses to all questions  
* Calculated scores per dimension  
* Timestamp and completion time  
* Device type (for potential analysis)

## **Validation Data Collection**

To build enterprise validity over time:

* Track test-retest reliability (offer users re-take after 2-4 weeks)  
* Correlate with outcomes if user reports job changes, satisfaction, etc.  
* Run factor analysis after 500+ completions to verify structure

# **LEGAL & COMPLIANCE NOTES**

## **What's Free to Use**

✅ **IPIP Items** — Public domain, free for any use including commercial ✅ **Big Five / OCEAN** — Public domain theory ✅ **Holland RIASEC** — Public domain theory ✅ **Original matrix/pattern items** — You create them, you own them

## **What Requires Care**

⚠️ **Clance Impostor Scale** — Requires permission for commercial use. Questions in this document are inspired by the construct but are original wording. ⚠️ **MBTI terminology** — "MBTI" is trademarked by The Myers-Briggs Company. Use "personality type" or your own terminology. You CAN say "INTJ-equivalent" or "similar to INTJ." ⚠️ **IQ claims** — Do not claim to measure "IQ" definitively. Use "estimated cognitive range" and include disclaimers.

## **EEOC Compliance (if used for hiring)**

If TalentRank is ever used in hiring decisions:

* Conduct adverse impact analysis (check for disparate impact by gender, race, age)  
* Document job-relatedness  
* Hire I/O psychologist to validate

For now (consumer product): Not required, but good to plan for.
